topics.name: The risk management process
topics.rationale: Cluster 1 is delivered first and holds both risk units. Identify, analyse, evaluate, treat and monitor is one method whether the risk is a fall from height or an insolvent subcontractor. BSBWHS513 is listed first in the cluster.
topics.teachingRule: BSBOPS504 Manage business risk applies the same five steps to commercial risk and teaches what is different - risk appetite, insurance, and the financial consequence of a treatment - not the method.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer runs the full cycle - identify, assess, control, review - applies the hierarchy of control rather than defaulting to PPE, and states how the effectiveness of a control is measured and when it is re-evaluated.
topics.benchmarkProvenance: draft 2026-09-09 - authored from the training.gov.au anchor, NOT yet validated by a subject matter expert

topics.name: Building and construction contracts and the obligations they create
topics.rationale: Nineteen of the twenty-seven units assume a contract sits behind the work. CPCCBC4009 Apply legal requirements sits in Cluster 2 and explains the contract as a source of obligation. CPCCBC4003 Select, prepare and administer a construction contract owns the mechanics of choosing and administering one; that content overlapped with nothing and is taught there in full.
topics.teachingRule: Estimating, site and technical units name the contract term bearing on their own output - a provisional sum, a variation clause, a practical completion date - and cite this topic rather than re-explaining contract law.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer identifies the contract type, states the obligations it creates for each party on time, cost and quality, and describes the variation and dispute provisions.
topics.benchmarkProvenance: draft 2026-09-09 - authored from the training.gov.au anchor, NOT yet validated by a subject matter expert

topics.name: Work health and safety duties on building and construction projects
topics.rationale: Seven units carry WHS duties as a legal obligation of the builder. Cluster 1 owns the RISK METHOD; CPCCBC4009 in Cluster 2 owns the DUTY - who holds it, to whom, and what breaching it costs.
topics.teachingRule: Site and technical units name the duty their activity triggers and the control that discharges it. Neither the method nor the legislation is restated.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer states the duty the WHS Act places on each duty holder on the project, how those duties overlap where parties share a workplace, and what consultation is required.
topics.benchmarkProvenance: draft 2026-09-09 - authored from the training.gov.au anchor, NOT yet validated by a subject matter expert

topics.name: Builder registration and licensing
topics.rationale: Who may lawfully contract to build, and in what class of work, is stated once in Cluster 2.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5007 cites the licence class and teaches the obligations attaching to holding it.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer states what work requires a licensed builder, the class of licence needed, and the consequence of carrying out licensable work without it.

topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC5019 cites the ACL where it bears on deposits, progress claims and refunds.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer states the consumer guarantees that apply to building work, the remedies available for a major and a minor failure, and that those guarantees cannot be contracted out of.

topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer states the employer duty to provide suitable duties and a return to work plan, who coordinates it, and how the plan is reviewed as capacity changes.

topics.rationale: Ten units extract information from the same drawing set. CPCCBC4003 in Cluster 2 is the earliest of them, and a contract is administered against the drawings and specification it incorporates.

topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer treats the drawings and specification as the contractual record, states which governs where they conflict, and identifies how a change is documented so the record stays current.

topics.name: The National Construction Code: structure, building classes and types of construction
topics.rationale: Cluster 3 is the codes cluster and is sequenced ahead of everything depending on it. Classification is the Code's first question, and CPCCBC4001 covers Class 1 and 10.

topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer classifies the building correctly, identifies its type of construction, and states which NCC volume and section govern it. It explains why classification determines the requirements that follow.

topics.rationale: Three families - written reports and memoranda, face-to-face verbal communication, and email - are one topic: choosing the channel that suits the message and leaving a record. CPCCBC4008 Supervise site communication and administration is the unit whose subject it is, and it opens Cluster 5.

topics.name: The hierarchy of control applied on site
topics.rationale: Elimination through to PPE is the control logic BSBWHS513 establishes in Cluster 1; the two units in this family apply it on a live site, and CPCCBC5010 in Cluster 5 is the earlier of them. Recorded as its own topic because the on-site application - who selects the control, who verifies it, what happens when a higher-order control is refused - is not what Cluster 1 teaches.
topics.teachingRule: CPCSUS5001 cites the hierarchy when writing sustainability controls and does not re-derive it.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer works down the hierarchy in order - elimination, substitution, isolation, engineering, administrative, PPE - justifies why a higher control is not reasonably practicable before moving down, and never presents PPE as the primary control.

topics.name: Building and construction methods and terminology
topics.rationale: The vocabulary is needed first where drawings are read, in Cluster 6.
topics.teachingRule: CPCCBC4014 restates in a line or two the terms its own subject needs, prompts the learner to define two of them from memory, then teaches its own method content in full. It does not re-explain the vocabulary from scratch. It still assesses the terminology in its own tool - applied, inside a question about its own subject rather than as a definition question, against the owner's benchmark.
topics.ownerBenchmark: A satisfactory answer uses the correct term for the element or method and applies it consistently to drawings, specifications and site instructions, so that the same component is named the same way by every party.

unownedTopicsNote: A requirement not appearing here overlapped nothing: it is unique to its unit, that unit teaches it, and no ruling was needed.
assessmentNote: ASSESSMENT IS PER UNIT. A ruling never removes a requirement from an applying unit's assessment tool - every unit is separately certified and evidences its own requirements in full, on its own mapped line, with no line naming another unit as its evidence. assessmentDepth governs DEPTH and FORM only: "applied" means assessed inside a question about this unit's own subject or carried by an observation item, against the owner's benchmark; "full" means this unit teaches and assesses its own subject matter in full. The register exists to keep those benchmarks consistent across the units that share a requirement, which is what Standard 1.5 validation tests.
